capabilities.description: The declared backend reach. ABSENT means zero reach — never "everything except a deny list". An installed application reaches nothing else: there is no backend command of its own to declare.

tables.description: The tables the application declares. Presence of capabilities.data declares the data.tables capability; declare an empty list when the application writes to no table.

highRisk.description: The consent-gated capability ids this package asks to use. Each one needs a per-application user consent before its first use.

version.description: The capability-contract major. It is versioned separately from manifestVersion and is additive within a major.

fredo.description: A semver RANGE such as ">=0.1.0" naming the Fredo versions the package accepts. "*" and an empty string are refused (engines_range_invalid); a well-formed range that excludes the running Fredo is host_incompatible.

document.description: Relative POSIX path to the package's HTML document (must end with '.html'); the host serves it with the bootstrap, the theme and the root element already injected.

module.description: Relative POSIX path to the package's ES module (must end with '.js') exporting mount(ctx). Import companions relatively — a bare specifier never resolves in an installed application's document.

table.description: One table the application declares for ITSELF. `source` is deliberately absent: a declared source projection would read Fredo's canonical tables (your own sessions and tool activity), which an installed application may never declare.

description: The manifest a Fredo compatibility package carries at its archive root as fredo-app.json. GENERATED from the Rust parser's own constants (applications/installed_apps/manifest.rs) — never edit it by hand. `additionalProperties` is false at every object level: an unknown key is refused, because a declaration this build does not read must never look accepted. NOT EXPRESSIBLE in JSON Schema and performed by `fredo-app check` in code: (1) whether engines.fredo's semver RANGE admits the running Fredo (the two failure families are distinct: a malformed range is engines_range_invalid, a well-formed range that excludes the host is host_incompatible); (2) the entry.* path rules (relative POSIX, no '..', no absolute/drive/scheme form, the documented extensions); (3) the declared table model (unique table and column names, a primary key naming declared columns); (4) entry_missing, which depends on the files actually packed. `capabilities` is optional and its absence means ZERO declared reach — never 'everything except a deny list'.

description.description: Optional. Omit the key when you have nothing to say — an unset optional is an absent key, never null.

displayName.description: The displayed name of the application.

id.description: Dot-separated lowercase segments; at most 96 characters. The eight built-in application ids are refused (id_reserved).

manifestVersion.description: The one manifest schema this build understands.
